ai.description: This slender, bright green pit viper reaches 60–80 cm. It features a distinct reddish-brown tail, a white lateral stripe along the ventrolateral scales, and a triangular head with heat-sensing pits.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Trimeresurus stejnegeri* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, thin white or yellowish stripe running along the lower edge of the scale rows on the flanks.
ai.habitat: Stejneger's pit viper inhabits humid, evergreen forests and bamboo thickets in the Indian subcontinent, typically found at elevations ranging from 500 to 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Stejneger's pit viper is primarily nocturnal, often positioning itself on low-hanging branches near streams to ambush unsuspecting frogs and small rodents.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Trimeresurus stejnegeri* is ovoviviparous, producing litters of 2–15 young. Breeding typically occurs during the spring and summer months.
ai.distributionRemarks: Stejneger's Pit Viper occurs in Northeast India, primarily within the Eastern Himalayas and Assam, inhabiting elevations ranging from near sea level up to 2,000 meters.
